cultural.vision_reason: A strip-woven kente cloth in black-and-white geometric checkerboard pattern, a hand-woven man's garment cloth characteristic of Akan/Ashanti weaving traditions.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man's garment, hand-woven in black and white cotton, composed of 22 hand-woven narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled alternately to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. Each narrow strip consists of a plain ground weave using white cotton in both warp and weft. A complicated pattern is introduced in the weft by a combination of continuous black lines that form one part of the check, and three discontinuous black designs that form the other part; a fourth design is used at the ends. The cloth has not been hemmed.
